item.title: Iran's IRGC declares 18 US firms 'legitimate targets'
item.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps on Tuesday issued a sweeping threat against 18 major American corporations, declaring them "legitimate targets" for retaliation and warning that strikes on their regional facilities could begin at 8:00 p.m. Tehran time on Wednesday, April 1.

item.title: Netanyahu says Israel destroying Iran's weapons capability
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declared on Tuesday evening that Israel had struck Iran and its "terror axis" with "10 plagues," delivering a televised Passover eve address that framed the ongoing war as a campaign of systematic dismantlement against Tehran's military infrastructure and regional proxy networks.

item.title: King Charles to visit US amid Trump-UK rift over Iran war
item.description:
Buckingham Palace confirmed on Tuesday that King Charles III and Queen Camilla will travel to the United States in late April for an official state visit, even as President Trump launched fresh attacks on Britain for refusing to join the military campaign against Iran.

The announcement came just minutes after Trump renewed his criticism of the UK and other European allies on Truth Social, telling them to "go get your own oil" from the Strait of Hormuz and warning that "the USA won't be there to help you anymore, just like you weren't there for us". Trump also urged Prime Minister Keir Starmer to "build up some delayed courage" and seize the strait, which has been largely closed since the Iran conflict began in late February.

item.title: Explosions rock Damascus as Israel intercepts Iranian missiles over Syria
item.description: Explosions echoed across the Syrian capital Damascus on Tuesday as Israeli air defense systems intercepted Iranian missiles passing through Syrian airspace, according to a report by Syrian state television carried by Reuters. The blasts underscore how Syria, despite avoiding direct involvement in the wider US-Israel war on Iran, is increasingly caught in the crossfire of a conflict now in its 32nd day.

item.title: Iran demands full end to war, rejects ceasefire talks
item.description:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi drew a firm line on Tuesday against any temporary pause in the month-long conflict with the United States and Israel, insisting Tehran will accept nothing less than a complete end to hostilities across the region. "We will not accept a ceasefire but rather seek a complete end to the war, not in Iran alone but in the entire region," Araghchi said, according to statements reported by Al Jazeera and confirmed by multiple outlets.

In an interview with Al Jazeera, Araghchi confirmed that messages have been exchanged with the U.S. — including with American envoy Steve Witkoff — but stressed that such contacts "do not mean that we are in negotiations". He added that Iran has "zero" trust in Washington's sincerity, citing the collapse of the 2015 nuclear deal.

item.title: Syria vows to stay out of US-Israeli war on Iran unless attacked
item.description:
Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa declared on Tuesday that Syria will not enter the ongoing US-Israeli military campaign against Iran unless the country comes under direct attack, positioning Damascus as a bystander in a regional conflict now in its second month.

"Unless Syria is targeted by any party, Syria will remain outside any conflict," al-Sharaa said during a speech at the Chatham House think tank in London, where he outlined his vision for the country's future. "We had enough war. We paid a large bill. We are not ready for another war experience".

item.title: UAE bans all Iranian nationals from entry and transit
item.description:
The United Arab Emirates has imposed a sweeping ban on all Iranian passport holders from entering or transiting through the country, with major carriers Emirates, Etihad Airways, and FlyDubai confirming the restriction in updated travel notices, according to Iran International. The directive, which took immediate effect, bars Iranian nationals regardless of visa category — including holders of valid residency, tourist, and visit visas.

The ban means Iranian nationals currently outside the UAE, including long-term residents, will be denied re-entry, with the restriction reflected in official immigration application responses. Emirates confirmed that Iranian nationals are "not permitted to enter or transit through the UAE," though it noted an exception for holders of Golden Visas, according to a statement reported by Al Arabiya.

item.title: China and Pakistan propose ceasefire as Chinese ships transit Hormuz
item.description: Three Chinese vessels have successfully transited the Strait of Hormuz, Beijing confirmed on Tuesday, marking the first major commercial shipping breakthrough since the waterway was effectively shut down following the start of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran a month ago.

item.title: New papers slash qubit estimates for codebreaking
item.description: Two research papers published on Monday dramatically lowered estimates of the quantum computing resources needed to break the encryption protecting cryptocurrencies, web browsers, and VPN connections, raising fresh urgency over the timeline for so-called "Q-Day" — the point at which quantum machines can crack widely used cryptographic systems.

item.title: Parker Solar Probe data challenges models of Sun's magnetic engine
item.description: NASA's Parker Solar Probe has upended longstanding assumptions about how the Sun accelerates charged particles, with new research showing that protons and heavy ions behave in fundamentally different ways during magnetic reconnection events near the solar surface.

item.title: Global stocks surge as Trump signals end to Iran war
item.description: Stock markets across Europe and India rallied on Wednesday as investors seized on comments from U.S. President Donald Trump suggesting the monthlong conflict in the Middle East could soon come to an end, triggering a wave of buying that lifted indexes by more than 2% in early trading.

item.title: Qubits needed to crack encryption fall 200-fold in under a year
item.description:
Three research papers published in the span of less than a year have dramatically reduced the estimated quantum computing resources needed to break modern encryption, compressing what many experts believed was a distant threat into a near-term challenge for governments, businesses, and the cryptocurrency industry.

The estimated number of physical qubits required to crack RSA-2048 encryption, the standard protecting most internet banking and digital certificates, has fallen from 20 million in 2019 to fewer than 100,000 under the latest architectures, according to a detailed analysis by The Quantum Insider published on Monday. In parallel, a Caltech and Oratomic team revealed on March 30 that fault-tolerant quantum computers could function with as few as 10,000 to 20,000 qubits, down from the millions previously thought necessary.

item.title: South Korea exports hit record $86B as global factories stockpile amid Iran war
item.description: South Korea's exports surged to a record $86.13 billion in March, while euro zone factory activity hit a 45-month high, as businesses worldwide rushed to stockpile materials amid supply chain turmoil from the conflict in the Middle East.

item.title: NASA set to launch Artemis II moon mission today
item.description: NASA is preparing to launch its Artemis II mission as early as Wednesday evening, sending four astronauts on the first crewed voyage toward the moon since Apollo 17 in December 1972. Among them is Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen, who will become the first non-American ever to travel beyond low Earth orbit.

item.title: BBC: Seizing Iran's uranium would be 'most complicated' special operation in history
item.description: President Donald Trump is weighing a military operation to extract roughly 1,000 pounds of enriched uranium from Iran, but nuclear and defense experts warn the mission could become one of the most complex and dangerous special operations ever attempted. The Wall Street Journal first reported the deliberations late last month, citing senior officials who said no final decision has been made.

item.title: New studies reveal how DNA motion and cell mechanics drive cancer
item.description: A burst of new research is reshaping how scientists understand cancer at its most fundamental level. Multiple studies published in recent weeks reveal that the physical behavior of DNA and the internal mechanics of cells play far larger roles in cancer development and spread than previously recognized, pointing to potential new therapeutic targets.

item.title: Trump to address nation Wednesday on Iran war exit
item.description: President Trump told reporters on Tuesday that the United States could end military operations against Iran "within two weeks, maybe two weeks, maybe three," his clearest indication yet that Washington is preparing to wind down the month-long conflict known as Operation Epic Fury. Trump is set to address the nation Wednesday evening with what the White House called "an important update" on the war.

item.title: Iran hits tanker off Qatar, strikes Kuwait airport as Gulf war widens
item.description: Iran launched cruise missiles at Qatar and struck Kuwait's international airport with drones early Wednesday, extending a wave of attacks on Gulf Arab states that has rattled energy markets and deepened pressure on Washington to broker a ceasefire more than a month into the conflict.

item.title: Trump claims Iran requested ceasefire; Tehran denies it
item.description:
President Donald Trump claimed on Wednesday that Iran's president had requested a ceasefire from the United States, posting the assertion on his Truth Social platform hours before a scheduled primetime address to the nation on the war in Iran. Trump conditioned any consideration of a pause in hostilities on Iran reopening the Strait of Hormuz, the critical waterway through which roughly a fifth of the world's oil normally flows.

"The Iranian president has just requested a CEASEFIRE from the United States of America!" Trump wrote, according to DW News. "We will determine when the Strait of Hormuz is accessible and free. Until that time, we are relentlessly targeting Iran, or as they say, reverting them to the Stone Age!"

item.title: NASA chief says 90% chance of proving ancient life on Mars
item.description: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman is steering the agency toward an ambitious new era of deep-space exploration, laying out plans for a permanent lunar base, a nuclear-powered Mars mission, and expressing strong personal conviction that evidence of ancient life on the Red Planet is within reach.
